prerequisites: Technical knowledge from the Bachelor's degree; no special prior knowledge in project management

learning_outcomes.text: Students acquire basic knowledge of project management and organizational forms in companies. They learn to successfully plan and control projects. They get to know the professional practice of their field and learn the methodical processing of a new technical task from professional practice.
Students can present project management methodology and apply it in their own projects. They familiarize themselves with a new task and deepen specific knowledge in this environment.

Students reflect on project management concepts in a situation-specific manner. These are considered in relation to the complex context in the respective organization and project phase and critically weighed against each other. Problems are solved with professional plausibility against the background of possible connections.

Students master the vocabulary, methods, and tools (e.g., MS Project, Excel) for the targeted execution of projects. They can apply these to projects from professional practice. They use professional methods to process their technical task.

Students master the systematics of project management and can independently acquire further literature. Students can independently classify new research results and verify hypotheses using suitable scientific methods.

Students can present the principles of project management using technical vocabulary. In addition, they learn to work in teams with the associated communication processes through group exercises and role plays. They can integrate into professional practice and communicate with colleagues and superiors within the framework of project work.

Students master the systematics of project management and can independently acquire further literature. They can apply this within the framework of their project work. They apply subject-specific skills and techniques to solve their project-specific tasks from professional practice.

syllabus_topics: Application of Project Management Methods for the execution of a practical project (preliminary study) and planning of a subsequent Bachelor's thesis
assessment_rules: The module is assessed based on a project report, which must be explained in a presentation. The grade is jointly awarded by the PM lecturer and the subject professor. The PM lecturer assesses the project management aspects (weighting: 1/3), and the subject professor assesses the subject-related parts (weighting: 2/3). The overall grade results from the weighted average of the two assessments. For the ungraded performance 'Project Week', successful participation in a project from the Project Week offering and the presentation of the results at the end of the Project Week are required. This proof of performance is issued by the supervisor of the respective project in the Project Week.
